events.title: Opera 2.0 publicly released
events.summary: Opera Software released Opera 2.0 for Windows in April 1996 — a compact alternative browser from Norway that prioritized speed and standards on modest hardware.
events.about: Opera became the browser power users and mobile pioneers reached for when IE and Netscape felt bloated. It pioneered features later copied everywhere: tabbed browsing, mouse gestures, built-in pop-up blocking, and a small install size for slow connections and early smartphones.

narrative.whyChosen: Opera proved independent browsers could survive and innovate outside the Netscape–Microsoft duopoly.
narrative.whyImportant: Its experiments with tabs, compression, and mobile browsing influenced Safari, Firefox, and Chrome.
narrative.problemSolved: Many users on slow dial-up or weak PCs needed a faster, configurable browser than the two dominant giants offered.
